slot.brief: Give the observed molar mass of a complex salt in solution (or its measured boiling point elevation) and ask to deduce the dissociation/association and hence the number of ions or the formula of the complex.

stem: The apparent molar mass of $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$ in dilute solution is $164.5$ g mol$^{-1}$; its true molar mass is $329$ g mol$^{-1}$. What is its degree of dissociation?

verdicts.working: The salt dissociates into 4 ions, so i = 1 + 3α. Also, i = 329/164.5 = 2. Hence α = (2 − 1)/3 = 1/3.

working:
$i=\dfrac{M}{M_{\mathrm{app}}}=\dfrac{329}{164.5}=2$
$\text{K}_3[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]\rightarrow 3\text{K}^+ + [\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}$
$i=1+3\alpha$
$2=1+3\alpha\implies \alpha=\dfrac{1}{3}=33\dfrac{1}{3}\%$

Independent check: The salt dissociates into 4 ions, so i = 1 + 3α. Also, i = 329/164.5 = 2. Hence α = (2 − 1)/3 = 1/3.
solution:
The van’t Hoff factor is $i=\dfrac{M}{M_{\mathrm{app}}}=\dfrac{329}{164.5}=2$. Since $\mathrm{K_3[Fe(CN)_6]}$ dissociates into 4 ions, $i=1+3\alpha$.
$$2=1+3\alpha\implies \alpha=\frac{1}{3}=33\dfrac{1}{3}\%$$
